Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. This will be the 70th all-time matchup between these two in-state rivals, with Florida leading the series 39-28-2 all time. The Gators are looking for their third straight victory in the rivalry. Florida has the opportunity in this one to not only win eight regular-season games for the first time since 2020, but also keep their counterparts from making a bowl game. It may not have been a pretty last couple of weeks for the Gators, but a chance to finish the season winning three straight, building momentum for the future, is a good starting point for year one under a new head coach. On the other hand, the Seminoles are coming off arguably their worst loss of the season at home, losing by 18 points to a 5-6 NC State team. Daniels is a volatile quarterback accounting for 27 total touchdowns this year (14 passing, 13 rushing) and 14 interceptions. Its offense seemed impossible to stop, hanging 52 on Ole Miss in Week 4. But inconsistency has been rampant across the team, with all four of Florida's losses coming by 16-plus points. Outside of that Ole Miss trouncing — a game that came off the back of a wildly emotional Rebels win over LSU — Florida has a negative point margin in SEC play. There are two big wins over Texas and Kentucky (both on the road) but also a one-score sweat over Vanderbilt at home. Florida is a mystery box each and every week. Florida's offensive line has been a root of the issue in an offense that's very much run-first. Early downs have become predictable, with the featured player being Jadan Baugh (960 yards, SEC-leading 16 rushing touchdowns). Quarterback Aaron Philo has been utilized well when healthy, rushing for almost 200 yards and three touchdowns over the past two games, and Florida converts regularly on late downs. Two major issues plague Florida's defense, and they've blown the floodgates open: it allows too many consistent chunk plays through the air and cannot get off the field on late downs. The Gators rank 125th nationally in third/fourth-down success rate (50.3%) and 121st in Passing Success Rate. Jayden Woods and Emmanuel Oyebadejo make up one of the SEC's most productive pass-rush duos, with 14 combined sacks (Oyebadejo notched two of his own last week). But when the rush isn't getting home, Florida's secondary struggles to contain production. The best of Florida gives you one of the best football teams in the country. But there's been more bad than good lately, and Florida's floor is the bottom third of the SEC. Florida State 's long nightmare is over as Mike Norvell finally got the axe. Not only that, but FSU already has its next head coach lined up: Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann. But until Schumann takes over, Rick Stockstill will lead the 'Noles as interim head coach. Under Stockstill, FSU is 2-1, with one-score wins over a free-falling Pitt (lost five of its last six) and Boston College, along with a 28-10 loss to NC State last week. Not super inspiring results, to say the least. Against NC State, Florida State gained just 36% of available yards and hit the Red Zone just once (on the opening drive). It put the ball in harm's way four times, fortunately recovering both fumbles but also throwing two interceptions. Quarterback Ashton Daniels is now up to 14 picks thrown on the year, the most among FBS arms. The run game has struggled without Ousmane Kromah (out for the year with an ankle injury), and the throw game has struggled without Duce Robinson (torn ACL). Four-star freshman Amari Thomas left early last week, and Tre Wisner hasn't played since Week 10. This is an offense limping to the finish line, with a quarterback doing everything he can as his eligibility runs out. The Seminoles don't have the horses to be effective in the Gus Malzahn-esque option system. Offensive struggle usually comes with a defensive slip (see: Ohio State ). FSU hasn't played a quality offense since Miami (43 points allowed in a pair of overtimes) and Louisville (44 allowed the week before). Since then, it's been a run of injured teams that didn't have much offensive prowess to begin with. Of course, FSU is capable of getting up for one more game against bitter rival Florida. These intrastate rivalries in the Sunshine State are packed with genuine vitriol, and this roster will do everything but roll over and die, especially since a good chunk of it is still Florida-grown. Florida is a six-point road favorite this Saturday, with an over/under of 53.5. Florida has been bad as a favorite this year, posting a 2-6 ATS record with three outright losses. Meanwhile, Florida State is 4-1-1 ATS as an underdog this season. This line remained unchanged since the lookahead line posted this summer for both the total and spread. Florida State's roster has been decimated. Its top weapons are out for the remainder of the season, and the two fill-ins in the backfield are both banged up. For a run-first team, losing that kind of firepower in the backfield is a massive handicap. With the Schumann era on the doorstep and with a roster missing significant portions of its lineup, this is a game Florida State might just be happy to get over with, even if it is against an in-state rival. Favorites have covered each of the last four in this series, with Florida running away with the last two meetings. The Gators are much healthier coming into this matchup with more stability in the coaching ranks heading into 2027. This is a numbers play. Anything at +7 or better is probably a bet on FSU, while anything under is all Florida. Pick: Florida -6 (-112, DraftKings | Play to -6.5)

Former Kentucky staffer Chase Heuke is also on the front office staff at Louisville. Of the former Wildcats, Wibberley has played the largest role for Louisville this season, starting eight of the first 11 games. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.1% completions, 2,448 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. four interceptions) threw one interception as UK went 7-1 in its first eight games. The Notre Dame transfer has been picked off three times, however, during the Wildcats’ current three-game losing skid. As UK played from behind in last week’s 28-14 loss at Missouri, Minchey, a 6-foot-2, 211-pound fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw a season-high 43 passes, completing 27 for 288 yards with no touchdowns and two picks. • The UK defense has struggled this season against the quarterback run game and Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz (67.5% completions, 2,739 yards, 20 touchdowns, four interceptions; 392 rushing yards, 11 touchdowns) is a more-than-capable runner. A 6-2, 215-pound junior from Pierre, South Dakota, Kienholz ran for a net-81 yards in a 44-17 win over Georgia Tech and has rushed for a net-40 yards or more in six other games. A transfer from Ohio State, Kienholz also has five games in which he has thrown for 300 yards or more, including last week’s 42-10 strafing of Pittsburgh, when he passed for 309 yards and five touchdowns vs. one interception. Advantage : Louisville Running backs • Kentucky running backs had a rough go in the loss to Missouri. UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (610 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) and backup Jason Patterson (504 yards, 5.8 yards a carry, three TDs) each left the Mizzou game early due to injuries. Barnes also lost a fourth-quarter fumble at the Missouri 13-yard line. • Louisville’s Isaac Brown (834 rushing yards, 7 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 19 catches, 177 yards, two touchdowns) missed last season’s Governor’s Cup rivalry game due to injury. As a freshman in 2024, Brown won the game’s Howard Schnellenberger MVP Award after carrying 26 times for 176 yards and two touchdowns in a 41-14 U of L rout of Kentucky at Kroger Field. Senior Keyjuan Brown (672 yards, 7 yards a carry, six TDs) has run for 50 yards or more in six straight games. In so doing, the 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, moved past Barion Brown (50 receptions for 628 yards in 2022) to claim UK’s freshman record for most catches and receiving yards in a season. TreyShun Hurry (45, 452, 3) and Lawayne McCoy (36, 640, six) are also productive. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (58 catches, 560 yards, three touchdowns) caught eight passes for 93 yards in the loss at Missouri. UK coach Will Stein said Monday that Wood’s status to play this week is “day to day.” If the ex-Madison Central standout cannot go, left guard Olaus Alinen will shift to right tackle and Jordan Knox will move into the vacated guard spot. • Louisville left tackle Lance Robinson was named Outland Trophy National Player of the Week after earning a 90 grade with three knockdown blocks in U of L’s 44-20 romp over Florida State on Oct. 9. Center Evan Wibberley , played last season for Kentucky after spending his first three college campaigns at Western Kentucky. The 6-3, 260-pound Lubin had two sacks vs. UK last season. At right end, former UK player Jerod Smith II has made 20 tackles with 1.5 sacks and 4.5 TFL. Tackle Demeco Kennedy (28 tackles, one sack, three TFL) is a Frederick Douglass High School product who played with UK nose guard Jamarrion Harkless at both Douglass and then Purdue. • With 87 stops, Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey is the second-leading tackler in the SEC. A 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player, Godfrey has made double-digit tackles in four games this year. SLB Sam Greene (34 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, an interception) made six tackles at Mizzou. • Louisville MLB Stanquan Clark (team-high 77 tackles, 1.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, five pass breakups, 2 QB hurries) has three double-digit tackles games this season. picks.source: USC Trojans On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: From a conference championship appearance, a playoff berth and a straight-up rivalry, there's a lot at stake for No. 15 USC Trojans' season finale vs. the No. 9 UCLA Bruins. Odds may be shifting the Trojans' way but these three factors can guarantee a upset victory. 1. Defense Flusters UCLA Quarterback Madden Iamaleava The Bruins might have Ty Dieffenbach listed as “probable,” but it could be more of a guise to avoid the outcome Florida State had in 2023. For now, Madden Iamaleava, the younger brother of Nico Iamaleava, is expected to start, and the Trojans' defense should be licking its chops. When the sophomore entered the game, he looked hesitant and unprepared. The result was a rough outing, failing to make a complete pass and rushing for negative yards. On top of his depth chart status at the start of the year, Iamaleava has little high school experience to lean on as well. Madden backed up Nico at Warren High (Downey, Calif.) from his freshman to sophomore year. He made a total of 17 appearances during that time, but it was a small sample size. Then in 2023, Madden became the full-time starter. In 13 games, he threw for 3,626 yards, 43 touchdowns and only four interceptions, per MaxPreps. He showed flashes of being a dynamic runner as well, rushing for 305 yards and three scores. A fallout at Warren led to a midseason transfer attempt to Long Beach Poly. Ultimately, Iamaleava did not play his senior year. Plus, the Bruins' offense has already been struggling under Dieffenbach – four interceptions in seven games, two of which came from Dieffenbach against Michigan in Week 12, No. 98 in points per trip inside the opponent’s 40-yard line and a lack of explosive plays despite having an excellent rushing attack. As great as coach Bob Chesney has been this season, it seems like a tall task to have the young Iamaleava ready on Nov. 28. Despite a slow start, USC’s defense came to play against a red-hot Maryland offense. Despite having a low pressure rate of 28 percent, the line was able to record four quarterback hits. The defensive front also disrupted the Terrapins’ run game with four tackles for loss (seven yards). More importantly, the secondary came away with three interceptions. With a lack of an outside threat, USC can focus on bringing the pressure from the interior and a blitzing nickelback. Desman Stephens II and Deven Bryant have done an excellent job leading the middle of the defense, and they will be huge in slowing down the Bruins' lead back, Wayne Knight. Taking all that into consideration, the Trojans defense can come away with three to four sacks and three turnovers in the contest. 2. Another Dominant Day on the Ground for Waymond Jordan and King Miller It appeared that Lincoln Riley was going to fall into old habits when trailing 14-13 to Maryland at halftime – get pass-happy, speed up the momentum and make questionable play calls. Fortunately, the USC offense got gritty with the run game, taking pressure off quarterback Jayden Maiava while providing an easy check-down option and milking the clock. The dynamic duo of Waymond Jordan and King Miller accounted for 140 of USC’s 184 rushing yards. Jordan – 18 carries, 70 yards, two touchdowns – looks healthy as ever, with his quick cuts and strong finishes. Miller – 10 carries for 70 yards – continues to shine as the explosive runner and is a huge plus as an easy pass option. It's also worth noting that Southern Cal is 8-1 when they rush for 100-plus yards and 0-2 when they rush for less than 100 – both of which were on the road. Riley has seemed to grow fond of the 12-personnel look and two-back backfield, which only opens up the passing game when the backfield duo is rolling. He needs to lean on it once again. Going against the Bruins' defense won't be an easy task, as the unit is No. 6 in rushing yards allowed per game (88.5) and No. 4 in yards per rush (2.7), but if USC can sustain drives with the run, they can tire out and punish this defense. With Miller as the lead rusher this time around, the two will combine for 120-plus yards and account for two scores on the day. 3. Double Digit Victory for the USC Trojans USC has won by double digits five times this season. While all five were at home, the Trojans won’t be dealing with the away-game narrative at the Rose Bowl. Similar to the Ohio State game, the defense will keep everything in front of them while flustering a young, backup quarterback. The offense will be willing to play a smash-mouth game while getting the ball to wideout Trent Mosley for explosive plays for a final score of 35-17. UCLA's Ty Dieffenbach is latest example of confusing injury reports
home.blurb: On Monday, the national reporting on the health status of UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach contained multiple contradictions. ESPN's Pete Thamel, for instance, wrote in a tweet that "Ty Dieffenbach isn't expected to be out long-term. While his status is uncertain for this week against USC, Dieffenbach is dealing with a minor hip injury. Dieffenbach is expected to be available for the College Football Playoff should UCLA clinch a bid." That piece of reporting veers in several different directions. When a player "isn't expected to be out long-term," that is generally viewed as news that an injury will be weeks instead of months or the full season. That does mean, however, that the injury carries short-term costs. If an injury isn't "long-term," it is short-term, so it exists. If an injury isn't short-term (meaning that the player is healthy enough to play his next game), there's no point or purpose in even saying whether the injury is long-term. Notice also how the reportage focuses on Ty Dieffenbach could be ready for the College Football Playoff in mid-December but also contains that oh-by-the-way part about maybe playing this week. All of this feels like a misdirection play, and it's understandable why UCLA might not be telling the exact truth. The Bruins have no incentive to do so, calling to mind the Florida State situation in 2023, when the Seminoles were left out of the playoff due to the injury to quarterback Jordan Travis. All of this aside, however, injury reports have become a source of confusion before this Dieffenbach situation at UCLA. USC football has featured plenty of situations in the Lincoln Riley era in which a player was abruptly announced as being out of a game when there were no outward indications of an injury absence during the week. Other players have been reported as having a chance to return on a given weekend only to miss that game and then multiple games after that, which meant that the original possibility of playing in Week X was never realistic. The Sooners have strung together three straight wins over Florida, Ole Miss, and Texas A&M after alternating wins and losses in each of their first nine games this year, the longest such streak in program history to open a season. The Sooners' 10th opponent out of 12 this fall will be the Missouri Tigers, who were either ranked or receiving votes in at least one major poll at kickoff. Only Oklahoma's opener against UTEP and last week's opponent, Texas A&M, were not ranked or receiving votes. This will be the 99th meeting between the two former conference rivals . The series is 68-25-5 in Oklahoma's favor, including a 9-2 record in the last 11 meetings, 21-3 in the last 24 meetings, and 23-7 in the last 30 meetings in Columbia. OU is 17-6 all-time against ranked Missouri teams. The Sooners and Tigers have played each other as members of the Missouri Valley Intercollegiate Athletic Association, the Big Seven, the Big Eight, the Big 12, and now in the SEC. Under Sooners head coach Brent Venables , OU is 1-1 against Missouri. The Tigers got the best of Oklahoma in their first meeting as SEC institutions in 2024, with a 30-23 win in Columbia. Then in 2025, Oklahoma returned the favor with a 17-6 victory in Norman. Since last season, OU has won five of its last six SEC road games (excluding a 27-24 win over No. 1 Texas in Dallas in 2024), including wins at Mississippi State and No. 25 Florida in 2026 and wins at South Carolina, No. 14 Tennessee, and No. 4 Alabama in 2025. Oklahoma's offense has found new life this month since Jason Witten was promoted from tight ends coach to interim offensive coordinator. Under Witten, the Sooners have averaged 25 points per game. OU's offense has done a much better job of playing complementary football, controlling the clock, running the football, and making life easier on the defense by keeping them off the field. As a result, the Sooners' defense has allowed an average of just 10 points per game over their last three contests. With only five drives of 10 or more plays in the first five games of the season, Oklahoma has had 18 such drives in the last six games. This includes a 20-play, 12:45 drive for a touchdown against Florida, the Sooners' longest such drive since 1972 and the longest by any SEC team this season. Third-down conversions have improved from 37% in the first eight games to 52% under Witten, and time of possession is averaging 36:08 per game (fifth in the country and best among Power Four teams during the stretch). Oklahoma quarterback John Mateer has played better in the Sooners' last three games than in the previous nine, scoring three touchdowns on 335 total yards in last week's 28-7 win over Texas A&M and three touchdowns on 337 total yards in the previous three games. His three highest rushing totals of the season have come in those last three games (56 yards at Florida, 70 vs. Ole Miss, 66 vs. Texas A&M). He has rushed for 192 of his 337 rushing yards in the three games Witten has called the plays. This includes both of his rushing touchdowns this season, running behind the same five offensive linemen in each of those three games: Michael Fasusi, Noah Best, Jake Maikkula, Heath Ozaeta, and E'Marion Harris. The Tigers' offense also includes dynamic receivers in Cayden Lee and Donovan Olugbode. Missouri has had a great season defensively, leading the SEC in turnover margin. However, the Tigers allow a lot of passing yards and have given up quite a few explosive plays this season. That means Mateer and Witten can get things done on offense if Oklahoma can protect the football as they have in the last five games, with just two total giveaways. The Sooners' defense is made up of all homegrown players who started their college careers in Norman. All 15 players who have started at least one game this season play on defense. Oklahoma's defense is top-20 in the country in third-down defense (27.4%, No. 3), first downs allowed (14.3 per game, No. 3), passing defense (163.1 ypg, No. 7), red-zone defense (72.0%, No. 8), total defense (284.6 ypg, No. 12), sacks (2.8 per game, No. 17), and scoring defense (17.9 ppg, No. 18). With Butkus Award semifinalist Owen Heinecke leading the Sooners' defense in tackles with 91, 11.5 for loss, as well as Kip Lewis, David Stone, and lockdown corner Courtland Guillory (36.2 passer rating allowed when targeted), Oklahoma will be looking to have a clean, tackling-focused, disciplined game in Columbia on Saturday.
